files.why: Add the framework-free BillingPeriod entity (id, name, start, end) plus a BillingPeriodSummary read model that carries per-period totals.
Add pure rules: does an invoice/appointment fall in a period's range, sum per-period totals, and project a period to its summary read model.
Add billingPeriodDtoSchema (snake_case, ISO date strings) as the server shape for periods; stays inside data/.
Map the billing-period DTO to/from the core BillingPeriod entity so DTOs never leak upward.
Add fetchBillingPeriods / fetchBillingPeriodById that validate the DTO and return core entities.
Add createBillingPeriod so finance can name/define a new period (a period is a persisted, named range).
Seed period data and add MSW handlers for /api/billing-periods so the feature has a working mock API.
Register /billing-periods and /billing-periods/:id, lazy-loading the two new views.
Load periods and expose each period's computed totals for the list view.
Assemble one period: its invoices (billing data) + in-range appointments via @slices/scheduling public API + totals from core rules.
List named periods with their per-period totals.
Show a single period: its grouped appointments, its invoices, and the totals.
Presentational per-period totals summary reused by the list rows and the detail header (same reason to change).
Add fetchAppointmentSummariesInRange(start,end) so billing can get 'appointments that happened in' a period without touching scheduling internals.
Expose the new in-range appointment read-model query on scheduling's public surface (the only legal cross-slice path).
Add a 'Billing periods' nav link; which routes appear in the shell is an app concern.
Cover the new pure period rules: range membership and per-period total aggregation.
Cover the new billing-period DTO<->core mapping round trip.

uncertain: Whether 'billing periods' should be a new top-level slice instead of living inside billing. I placed it in billing because it changes for billing/finance reasons and is about invoices; a new slice would touch the CODEOWNERS-protected architecture.config.ts (adding to `slices`) and its generated configs — reserved for architecture review, so I avoided it.

billing/index.ts: I left it unchanged because periods appear to be internal to billing and routes are already re-exported. If the app-level ClientOverview (or another slice) must show periods, index.ts would need to expose a BillingPeriod read model + query.
billing/core/policy.ts: only needed if a period has a lifecycle (open/closed/locked so invoices can't move between periods). The request doesn't mention it, so I left policy out.

BillingPeriodTotalsCard.vue: if the totals turn out to render differently on the list vs the detail page (two reasons to change), it should stay inline in each view rather than be one shared component (constitution rule 6).

Whether a period's appointment set should come from a scheduling range query (what I assumed) or be derived from the appointmentIds of the invoices already in the period — the latter would reuse the existing fetchAppointmentSummaries(ids) and need no scheduling change.
questions: What defines membership: does a period group invoices by their issue/raised date, appointments by their date, or both independently? This directly shapes the core range-membership rules.
Are billing periods persisted, finance-named entities (implying create/edit/delete + a server endpoint), or just an ad-hoc date-range filter over existing data? I assumed persisted and named.
Which money total(s) do finance want per period — subtotal, tax, grand total, count of invoices/appointments, and does status (draft/void) affect what's counted?
Do periods need a lifecycle (close/lock a period so its contents freeze), which would add core policy rules and a mutation?
Can periods overlap or must they tile the calendar contiguously, and is currency assumed single per period (existing invoices are per-invoice currency)?
Should the client overview / other slices see periods, or is this purely a new billing area?
